target_customer: Designers and design teams working in Photoshop, Illustrator, Sketch and similar tools
problem: Designers shared files in giant folders with no version history, so teams could not track or compare revisions the way developers do with Git.
business_model: Freemium SaaS for design version control and sharing
product_category: Version control and collaboration for design files

founders.name: Shravan Reddy
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in the YC launch post and as a founder in The Next Web 2015 coverage. The YC company page lists only Min Ming Lo.

founders.name: Min Ming Lo
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says the Google internship exposed the problem. The YC page describes engineering, design and product roles.

exit.reason: Terms were not disclosed. The product was to be integrated into Dropbox over the next year with a migration path for users.

technical_complexity.rationale: Rendering and diffing visual versions of many binary design formats (over 50 by 2015) is harder than ordinary file sync.

defensibility.rationale: File history created some lock in, but Dropbox was the natural host for the same wedge and the product depended on desktop file sync.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dropbox bought the company in January 2015 to add version control for visual work, after Pixelapse had worked with Dropbox sync.

market_need_then: The YC launch post of February 2013 describes teams dumping design files into one giant folder with no history. Demand was real but narrow to design teams.

branding.domain_note: Used pixelapse.com; the site returned a service error at fetch time.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as GitHub for designers in YC and press coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch, Fast Company and the YC blog, but no source shows brand driven growth or community.

outcome_analysis: Pixelapse launched publicly in February 2013 as GitHub style version control for designers, joined StartX in 2012 and was acquired by Dropbox in January 2015 for an undisclosed price. The outcome was a small acquisition that folded the product into Dropbox, so it counts as a modest exit rather than a failure. The directory marks it Inactive because the standalone product was absorbed.
notes: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights), which reports $20K total over two rounds including the acquisition; the seed amount and investors are not given, and TechCrunch described the seed as undisclosed. The YC page lists a January 26, 2015 report while The Next Web gives January 27, 2015; month recorded. A startup history site places the end of the standalone product around 2016, unverified. The YC launch post is dated February 13, 2013, so the product launched after the Winter 2012 batch. Product Hunt threads ask about LayerVault but are undated in the results, so no competitor is recorded.
